hero_subtitle: The Ochre City of Palaces, Vibrant Souks, Secret Gardens & Endless Desert Gateways.

overview.title: Welcome to the Ochre City
overview.p1: Marrakech is an intoxicating sensory feast. Framed by the snow-capped Atlas Mountains, this imperial city effortlessly blends ancient Berber heritage with sophisticated contemporary luxury. From the bustling labyrinth of Medina souks to serene hidden patios in century-old riads, Marrakech is Morocco's ultimate cultural capital.
overview.p2: Whether you are wandering through Yves Saint Laurent's Jardin Majorelle, watching storytellers at Jemaa el-Fnaa as dusk falls, or heading into the nearby Agafay Desert for a night under the stars, Marrakech promises an unforgettable journey.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Marrakech
places.subtitle: Iconic landmarks, royal palaces, and historical gardens you cannot miss during your trip.

jemaa.title: Jemaa el-Fnaa & Souks
jemaa.desc: The beating heart of Marrakech, an open-air theater and labyrinth of artisan souks.

majorelle.title: Jardin Majorelle & YSL
majorelle.desc: A peaceful botanical haven famous for its cobalt blue villa.

bahia.title: Bahia Palace
bahia.desc: A masterpiece of Moroccan architecture featuring painted ceilings and zellige courtyards.

ben_youssef.title: Ben Youssef Madrasa
ben_youssef.desc: An ancient Islamic college and a jewel of Arab-Andalusian art.

saadian.title: Saadian Tombs
saadian.desc: Richly decorated mausoleums with Carrara marble in the Kasbah district.

elbadi.title: El Badi Palace
elbadi.desc: Grand ruins of a 16th-century palace home to nesting storks.

jardin_menara.title: Menara Gardens
jardin_menara.desc: A historic 12th-century olive orchard featuring a large water basin and a green-roofed pavilion.

dar_el_bacha.title: Dar El Bacha
dar_el_bacha.desc: A stunning 1910 palace showcasing Moorish architecture and the famous Bacha Coffee.

koutoubia.title: Koutoubia Mosque
koutoubia.desc: The iconic minaret of this 12th-century mosque stands 77 meters tall.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan to discover the essential sights without rushing through the city.

detailed_itinerary.day1_tab: Day 1 — The Heart of the Medina
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start at the Koutoubia gardens for soft morning light on the minaret, then stroll into Jemaa el-Fnaa while the square is still calm and easy to navigate.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Get lost in the vibrant artisan souks toward Ben Youssef Madrasa. Admire its intricate marble and stucco courtyard, then continue browsing spice and leather shops.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Return to Jemaa el-Fnaa as food stalls light up and the square turns into a magical open-air theatre. Enjoy dinner at a rooftop terrace with panoramic views.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Arrive early at Bahia Palace to beat the tour groups, then take a short walk to the Saadian Tombs located in the historic Kasbah neighborhood.
detailed_itinerary.day2_a: Afternoon — El Badi or Jardin Majorelle
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Choose El Badi Palace for grand open-air ruins and nesting storks, or head to Gueliz for Jardin Majorelle and the Yves Saint Laurent Museum.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Unwind in a peaceful riad courtyard or reserve a cozy spot at one of Marrakech's high-end Moroccan fine dining venues.
detailed_itinerary.day3_tab: Day 3 — Day Trip or Free Time
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Day Trip Departure or Menara
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Head out on an excursion to the High Atlas Mountains, Agafay Desert, or Ouzoud Waterfalls. Alternatively, enjoy a peaceful morning walk through the Menara Gardens.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Back in the city, revisit favorite souk stalls, sip coffee at Dar El Bacha, or indulge in a traditional Moroccan spa and hammam treatment.
detailed_itinerary.day3_e: Evening — Last Night in the Ochre City
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Enjoy a final glass of fresh mint tea on a rooftop lounge as sunset colors paint the city skyline.

directory.subtitle: Legendary palaces, charming boutique riads, or peaceful sanctuaries: explore our top recommended addresses for an unforgettable stay in Marrakech.

booking_banner.title: Explore All Places to Stay in Marrakech

eat.title: Best Restaurants & Rooftops
eat.subtitle: Handpicked culinary experiences with top guest reviews

nomad.title: Nomad Marrakech
nomad.desc: A trendy rooftop terrace overlooking Spice Square, serving light local cuisine with a modern twist.

jardin.title: Le Jardin
jardin.desc: A lush 16th-century courtyard filled with greenery and banana plants, offering authentic tagines in a tranquil atmosphere.

fassia.title: Al Fassia
fassia.desc: Run entirely by women, famous for its slow-cooked shoulder of lamb and rich traditional pastilla recipes.

moha.title: Dar Moha
moha.desc: Refined Moroccan gastronomy served around a tranquil courtyard pool in Pierre Balmain's former palace.

bacha.title: Bacha Coffee
bacha.desc: An iconic 1930s coffee room offering fine Arabica coffees and French pastries in an opulent palace setting.

elfenn.title: El Fenn Rooftop
elfenn.desc: A stylish rooftop lounge featuring panoramic Koutoubia views, signature cocktails, and gourmet tapas.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: Walking is best inside the Medina. For longer journeys, take yellow "Petit Taxis" and ask the driver to use the meter (compteur) before starting.

bargain.title: Souk Bargaining
bargain.desc: Haggling is part of the experience! Start at roughly 50% of the initial price and keep negotiations friendly and lighthearted.

water.title: Stay Hydrated
water.desc: Marrakech temperatures can soar, especially in summer. Stick to bottled water and enjoy fresh orange juice in Jemaa el-Fnaa.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Marrakech
daytrips.subtitle: Rent a car, hire a private driver, or join a small tour to reach these stunning destinations in a single day.

atlas.title: Atlas Mountains & Imlil
atlas.desc: Traditional Berber villages, valley treks, and alpine scenery about 1.5 hours from Marrakech.

agafay.title: Agafay Stone Desert
agafay.desc: Sunset camel rides, quad biking, and dinner under the stars, just 40 minutes from town.

ouzoud.title: Ouzoud Waterfalls
ouzoud.desc: Morocco's tallest waterfalls surrounded by lush greenery and playful Barbary macaques.

essaouira.title: Essaouira Coast
essaouira.desc: Fresh sea breeze, historical ramparts, and grilled seafood along the Atlantic coast.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Marrakech?
q1.answer: 3 to 5 days allows you to explore the Medina, palaces, and gardens at an enjoyable pace, with time left for an excursion to the High Atlas or Agafay Desert.

q2.question: Is Marrakech safe for international tourists?
q2.answer: Yes, Marrakech is generally very safe for travelers. As in any major tourism city, keep an eye on your belongings in crowded souks and agree on taxi prices upfront.

q3.question: What currency is used and can I pay by credit card?
q3.answer: Morocco uses the Moroccan Dirham (MAD). Cards are accepted at most hotels, fine restaurants, and larger shops, but carrying cash is essential for souks, taxis, and small cafes.

q4.question: How do I get from Marrakech Menara Airport to the Medina?
q4.answer: RAK airport is only 15 minutes away. Official taxis, pre-booked airport transfers, and local buses are all readily available right outside the arrivals terminal.
